sources_consulted.summary: OpenSpec=delta living-doc + propose/apply/archive; Spec Kit=/specify //plan //tasks phases; Kiro=EARS-notation requirements.md/design.md/tasks.md; BMAD=agent-as-code personas. Diverge on execution orchestration vs spec breadth vs brownfield change mgmt.

Neither Spec Kit nor OpenSpec document mature requirement-ID/traceability, live-code drift detection, formal change control, or state tracking - conceptual not shipped. Confirms this category commonly lacks exactly what SpecKiwi already has (REQ IDs, validation, mutation guards).

MCP 2025-06-18: structuredContent+outputSchema, elicitation/create (accept/reject/cancel), resource_link objects, _meta fields. Shifts servers from one-shot text to schema-validated interactive workflows.

Two error paths: protocol errors vs tool-execution errors (isError flag) - conflating them is the #1 mistake. stdout=JSON-RPC only, stderr=logs. Use McpError w/ codes like InvalidParams so clients react programmatically. MCP Inspector for debugging.

MCP RC: full JSON Schema 2020-12 (oneOf/anyOf/allOf/refs) tool schemas; W3C Trace Context via _meta for cross-SDK/gateway trace correlation; error code standardized -32002->-32602; server/discover capability method; list results carry ttlMs+cacheScope.

Agents are first-class CLI consumers: stable VERSIONED --json schema, distinct documented exit codes (0 ok/1 user/2 transient/3 validation/4 confirm), errors as JSON on stderr, schema <command> introspection, NDJSON streaming. If you cannot promise stability, your --json is theater.

sources_consulted.ref: Agent audit trail / checkpoint (IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail, AgentCenter, LangGraph)
sources_consulted.summary: Emerging std: hash-chained (SHA-256) append-only JSONL ledger, normalized keys (agent_id/action/outcome/trust). JSONL=RECOMMENDED export. Checkpoint AFTER unit completes (never before). LangGraph checkpointer=resumable threads.
EARS templates (When/While/Where/If-Then + ubiquitous SHALL) turn fuzzy stories into testable machine-readable acceptance criteria. Kiro auto-generates AC in EARS; forces edge-case decisions.
Gap analysis MUST be bidirectional: requirements with no downstream link=untested; artifacts with no source requirement=scope creep. Bidirectional catches coverage gaps AND test-suite bloat.
Progress notifications for long tools, cursor pagination (nextCursor->null at end), SEP-1686 task primitive call-now/fetch-later + tasks/list paginated. Prevents timeouts on big targets/validate.

registerTool supports outputSchema (validated before result leaves server), annotations {readOnlyHint,destructiveHint,idempotentHint}, isError:true returns (tool failures resolve as ordinary results, not thrown) with actionable text e.g. Known ids: .... Zod/ArkType supported.

best_practices.claim: Tool outputs should ship structuredContent + a declared outputSchema, not just a JSON string inside TextContent, so agents get validated machine-parseable results.
Mutation vs read tools must be distinguished via annotations (readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint) so agents/clients can gate risky writes.
Separate protocol errors from tool-execution errors; return tool failures as isError:true with recovery-actionable text rather than throwing; use standard JSON-RPC codes (-32602 Invalid Params).
Agent-native CLIs need a stable, versioned --json schema, distinct documented exit codes, JSON errors on stderr, and a schema-introspection command; unstable --json is worthless to agents.
Agent audit/workflow logs should be append-only JSONL with hash-chaining (SHA-256) and normalized record fields for tamper-evident, queryable trails.
Checkpoints must be written AFTER a unit of work succeeds (never before) to guarantee safe resume; resumable per-thread state is the norm (LangGraph checkpointer).
Acceptance criteria in EARS templates become testable + machine-readable, surfacing edge-case decisions early.
Traceability gap analysis must be bidirectional - flag both requirements with no downstream links (untested) and artifacts with no source requirement (scope creep).

findings.claim: SpecKiwi MCP tools likely still return JSON inside TextContent; adopting structuredContent + declared outputSchema gives agents validated, drift-proof results (the 2025-06 baseline).
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Add outputSchema+structuredContent to validate_spec/summarize_target/list_requirements/get_requirement; keep TextContent JSON for back-compat.

findings.claim: Mutation tools (add_requirement, update_status, repair-collisions, retarget) are indistinguishable from reads to a client without annotations; annotations let agents gate destructive writes and pair with existing dry-run.

Diagnostics quality hinges on separating protocol errors from tool-execution errors: return recoverable failures as isError:true with actionable text (e.g. unknown target X; known: v2.3.0, v3.0.0) instead of throwing, and map to stable codes (SRS-E### / JSON-RPC -32602).
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: isError result envelope with next-action hints + documented error-code catalog shared across CLI+MCP.

findings.claim: When an agent hits ambiguity (no active target, ambiguous REQ reference, duplicate-ID keep/rename choice), erroring out breaks the loop; MCP elicitation lets the server ask mid-call and continue.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Elicitation for missing active-target and collision keep/rename selection instead of hard failure.

findings.claim: Agent-native CLI table stakes are frequently missing: a stable VERSIONED --json schema, distinct documented exit codes (0/1/2/3/4), JSON errors on stderr, and a schema <command> introspection command - without these, agents parse prose and retry.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Versioned JSON schema contract + exit-code taxonomy + speckiwi schema <cmd> + JSON-on-stderr errors.

findings.claim: SpecKiwi already has workflow JSONL; the industry direction is tamper-evident hash-chained (SHA-256) append-only ledgers with normalized fields and a verifier - turning the log from advisory into an auditable, resumable SSOT.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: speckiwi workflow verify (hash-chain integrity) + normalized event schema aligned to AAT.

findings.claim: Long agent pipelines need safe resume: checkpoint AFTER each unit succeeds, expose a resumable state object; kiwi-pm-style runners benefit from a first-class CLI/MCP checkpoint-and-resume surface rather than ad-hoc .kiwi/ files.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: get_run_state/resume_run MCP tools + CLI speckiwi run status/resume reading the workflow ledger.

findings.claim: Acceptance criteria are the weakest link in most markdown-SSOT tools; EARS templates make AC testable+machine-readable and force edge-case decisions - a natural validation lint SpecKiwi could own vs. free-text AC.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: EARS-form lint diagnostic (SRS-W###) + optional AC scaffolding into When/While/Where/If-Then.

findings.claim: Traceability value comes from BIDIRECTIONAL gap analysis; a links-check that only verifies forward links misses scope creep - artifacts/code/tests with no source requirement are as risky as untested requirements.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: links check reporting orphaned requirements (no downstream) AND orphaned trace targets (no upstream REQ) + coverage-gap summary.

findings.claim: OpenSpec delta model (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED proposals against a living doc, propose->apply->archive) is the change-control primitive competitors are converging on; SpecKiwi SRS-change-protection could expose a reviewable change-proposal/diff object.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Structured SRS change-proposal (delta) object + speckiwi diff/review before apply.

findings.claim: Large targets risk MCP timeouts on validate/list; cursor pagination (nextCursor) + progress notifications, and eventually the SEP-1686 call-now/fetch-later task primitive, keep big-repo operations responsive.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Cursor pagination on list_requirements/list_completed_work + progress notifications on validate/doctor.

findings.claim: Observability is moving toward W3C Trace Context in _meta so a single requirement operation correlates across CLI, MCP, and downstream tools; this makes multi-agent pipeline debugging tractable.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Emit trace/span id in _meta and in workflow JSONL so CLI+MCP+pipeline events join on one trace.
